{
  "root_cause": "The modal's click listener treats any click inside the modal as a close action because the overlay element has the close-trigger attribute, causing a space‑activated checkbox click to bubble up and close the dialog.",
  "repair_strategy": "Update the onClick handler to close the modal only when the clicked element is the overlay (has class 'modal__overlay') or the explicit close button (id 'modal-close'), ignoring interactions with internal form controls.",
  "edits": [
    {
      "path": "lib/src/index.js",
      "sha256": "0db2038c36c8c8c4730018c0ea419249e45923efa8315729f12b4d8da0d5fa2c",
      "before": "    onClick (event) {\n      if (event.target.closest(`[${ this.config.closeTrigger }]`)) {\n        event.preventDefault()\n        event.stopPropagation()\n        this.closeModal(event)\n      }\n    }",
      "after": "    onClick (event) {\n      const closeTriggerEl = event.target.closest(`[${ this.config.closeTrigger }]`);\n      if (closeTriggerEl && (closeTriggerEl.classList.contains('modal__overlay') || closeTriggerEl.id === 'modal-close')) {\n        event.preventDefault()\n        event.stopPropagation()\n        this.closeModal(event)\n      }\n    }"
  },
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Pressing Space on the weekly digest checkbox will toggle its checked state while keeping the preferences dialog open (aria-hidden remains false) and focus retained inside the dialog.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "Accidentally preventing close actions for legitimate close-trigger elements if the selector logic is incorrect.",
    "Potential regression if other parts of the application rely on the previous behavior of closing the modal on any internal click."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "Verify that pressing Space on the checkbox toggles its value and the dialog stays open (aria-hidden false).",
    "Verify that clicking the overlay or the close button still closes the dialog.",
    "Verify that keyboard navigation (Tab, Escape) continues to work as expected.",
    "Verify that form submission or other interactions within the dialog are not adversely affected."
  ]
}

We need to analyze the problem.

From environment: we have a test where step sequence:

Step 0? Actually they list frozen journey requirements:
- Action seek selector "#open"
- Press Enter -> expects aria-hidden false on prefs-modal and focus on #weekly
- Press Space -> expects same as above plus form-data digest includes ["weekly"]

But observed failure occurs at step index 2 (the space press), where expected assertions fail: after pressing space on #weekly (checkbox), they expect aria-hidden false (still open) and digest value ["weekly"]. However observed shows aria-hidden "true"? Let's look at observed.after details: In failed step after pressing space, they gave after element info about button #open? Wait they show after bbox etc referencing #open again? That seems odd. They likely captured after state but maybe they incorrectly reported because the modal closed causing focus to go back to button #open. Indeed after pressing space on checkbox, the modal closed (aria-hidden true) and focus returned to #open. So the issue: pressing space on a checkbox inside the modal also triggers the modal close? Possibly because the modal library treats any keydown space on any element inside modal as triggering close? Look at micromodal code: It adds keydown listener on document (via addEventListeners) that calls onKeydown(event). In onKeydown, they check if event.keyCode === 27 (Esc) close modal; if event.keyCode === 9 (Tab) retainFocus. They do NOT handle space. So why would space close? Maybe because the checkbox itself when activated via space triggers a click event? Actually pressing space on a checkbox triggers click event (which toggles). The modal library also has click listener on modal (via addEventListeners: modal.addEventListener('click', this.onClick)). onClick checks if event.target.closest(`[${ this.config.closeTrigger }]`) then close modal. The closeTrigger is data-micromodal-close attribute. In the HTML, the close button #modal-close has that attribute, also the overlay div has data-micromodal-close. The checkbox does NOT have that attribute, so clicking on checkbox should not close. But maybe the click event bubbles up to the modal overlay? The overlay has data-micromodal-close attribute, so clicking anywhere inside modal (including checkbox) will bubble up to overlay? Actually the overlay is a div wrapping the modal container; clicking inside the modal container will still be inside overlay because overlay is position fixed inset:0 and contains modal container. The click listener is on modal element (the outer div with class modal). They attach listener to this.modal (the modal div). When clicking inside, event.target may be checkbox, but event.target.closest('[data-micromodal-close]') will look up the DOM for an ancestor with that attribute. The overlay div has that attribute, and it is an ancestor of the checkbox (since checkbox is inside modal container which is inside overlay). So clicking the checkbox will cause the click to bubble up to modal div, and the closest attribute will find the overlay, triggering closeModal. That explains why pressing space (which triggers click) closes modal.

Thus fix: modify the click handler to ignore clicks that originate from form controls (like checkbox, radio, button, etc.) Or more specifically, ensure that clicking on elements that are not the close trigger does not close. The current logic already checks closest closeTrigger, but due to overlay having that attribute, any click inside modal will match. To prevent this, we should not attach click listener to the modal overlay; instead attach to the modal container? Actually typical approach: close on click of backdrop (overlay) and close button, but not on inner content. In micromodal, they attached click listener to modal element (the outer div with class modal). Then they check if target closest closeTrigger. Since overlay also has that attribute, they rely on the fact that clicking on overlay will have target being overlay itself (or something inside overlay but not having closeTrigger?). Wait overlay has attribute data-micromodal-close, so clicking on overlay will have target with that attribute, thus closest returns overlay -> close. Clicking on inner content (like checkbox) will bubble up; the closest will find overlay because overlay has attribute, causing close. This is a bug in micromodal version used.

Fix: We can change the HTML to remove data-micromodal-close attribute from overlay, and keep it only on the close button and maybe the backdrop? Actually we need close on overlay click but not on inner content. So we need to differentiate: we could keep attribute on overlay but modify JS to check that event.target is the overlay itself (i.e., event.target.hasAttribute) rather than closest. Simpler: remove data-micromodal-close from overlay, and keep on close button and maybe on backdrop? But we need close when clicking outside the modal container (i.e., on overlay). If we remove attribute from overlay, clicking on overlay will not trigger close. So we need another way: maybe we can keep attribute on overlay but change JS to check event.target === this.modal? Actually the modal variable refers to the outer div with class modal (which includes overlay and container). Click on overlay: target is overlay div (which is a child of modal). Click on container: target is something inside container. Both are children of modal. So we cannot differentiate by target alone.

Alternative: Change HTML structure: move data-micromodal-close attribute to the overlay only, and not to the close button? But we need close button too. Could have both overlay and close button have attribute, but we need to ignore clicks that originate from inside modal container. We could check if event.target.closest('.modal__container') is null (i.e., click is outside container, i.e., on overlay). Then close. So modify onClick: if event.target.closest(`[${ this.config.closeTrigger }]`) && !event.target.closest('.modal__container') then close. But we must keep changes minimal.

Given we can only edit source files provided: index.html or lib/src/index.js. Changing HTML might be easier: remove data-micromodal-close from overlay and keep on close button only, and also maybe add attribute to overlay for close via click? Actually we need close when clicking overlay; we could instead add a click listener directly on overlay element in HTML using onclick? Not possible without JS.

Better to adjust JS: modify onClick to check if the closest element with closeTrigger is the overlay (i.e., not inside modal container). We can detect if the closest element with closeTrigger is also the modal's overlay (maybe by checking if it has class 'modal__overlay'). Since overlay has class 'modal__overlay'. So we can change condition to: const closeTriggerEl = event.target.closest(`[${ this.config.closeTrigger }]`); if (closeTriggerEl && closeTriggerEl.classList.contains('modal__overlay')) { this.closeModal(event); } Also we need to close when clicking the close button (which does not have that class). So we need to also close if closeTriggerEl is the close button (id modal-close). So condition: if (closeTriggerEl && (closeTriggerEl.classList.contains('modal__overlay') || closeTriggerEl.id === 'modal-close')). That will close on overlay or close button, but not on inner content.
